name: SER120 DB3/DB4
question: Does low-dose desmopressin nasal spray reduce nocturnal voids compared with placebo in adults with nocturia?

design.population: 1,333 adults aged at least 50 years with at least 2.16 nocturnal voids per night during screening were included in the pooled intent-to-treat analysis.
design.description: Pooled analysis of two multicenter, double-blind randomized trials
design.locator: Full text, Results, p 608; Table 1, p 606

verdictNote: Both pooled coprimary endpoints favored each dose; 0.83 mcg responder endpoint was significant only after pooling.
takeaway: In pooled DB3/DB4 intent-to-treat data, desmopressin nasal spray 0.83 and 1.66 mcg reduced nocturnal voids and increased 50% responder rates versus placebo over 12 weeks; the 0.83 mcg responder endpoint was significant only in the pooled analysis.

reports.label: Pooled DB3/DB4 analysis
reports.citation: Kaminetsky J, Fein S, Dmochowski R, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of SER120 Nasal Spray in Patients with Nocturia: Pooled Analysis of 2 Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo Controlled, Phase 3 Trials." *J Urol.* 2018;200(3):604-611. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2018.04.050
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 605

results.measure: Mean change in nocturnal voids per night over 12 weeks
results.note: Pooled ITT least-squares mean change; n=439 and n=446. No between-group estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 1A and Results, pp 607–608

results.measure: Mean change in nocturnal voids per night over 12 weeks
results.note: Pooled ITT least-squares mean change; n=448 and n=446. No between-group estimate or confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 1A and Results, pp 607–608

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in nocturnal voids, 1.66 mcg
results.note: Pooled ITT; denominator n=439 and n=446. Responder numerators and confidence intervals not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 1B and Results, pp 607–608

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in nocturnal voids, 0.83 mcg
results.note: Pooled ITT; denominator n=448 and n=446. Results text gives P=0.0159; abstract gives P=0.0227. Responder numerators and confidence intervals not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 1B and Results, pp 607–608

results.endpoint: Impact of Nighttime Urination score, 1.66 mcg
results.measure: DB4 INTU overall impact score, least-squares mean change from baseline
results.note: Higher dose versus placebo P=0.0255 in Results text; Figure 2 caption gives P=0.0225. No confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Figure 2 and Results, p 608

results.endpoint: Time from bedtime to first nocturnal void
results.measure: Pooled ITT least-squares mean change, minutes

results.endpoint: Nights with at most one nocturnal void
results.measure: Pooled ITT least-squares mean change in percentage of nights per patient
results.note: Table 2 row heading reads one or more, but Methods and Results define this endpoint as one or fewer nocturnal voids. No between-group confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 606; Results, p 608; Table 2, p 609

harms.label: Hyponatremia
harms.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 606; Safety, pp 609–610
harms.note: Safety population. Protocol definition: serum sodium ≤125 mmol/L regardless of symptoms or <130 mmol/L with symptoms. All five high-dose cases were older than 65 years.

harms.label: Nasal discomfort
harms.note: Treatment-emergent adverse event; pooled safety population.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Treatment-emergent adverse event; pooled safety population.

harms.label: Adverse-event discontinuation
harms.value: 80/1,356 (5.9%) across pooled safety population, regardless of causality
harms.note: Arm-specific counts not reported in the main text.

delivery.label: Randomized treatment
delivery.value: Intranasal SER120 1.66 mcg, 0.83 mcg, or placebo as a single spray in either nostril nightly before bedtime for 12 weeks; study assessments every 2 weeks. No fluid restriction or behavioral therapy was imposed.
